clue.text: Figure prat out, one for some drug-users to avoid

definitions.text: one for some drug-users to avoid

indicators.note: something put out of place is disordered, so the preceding words are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone tells a figure-of-fun to clear off because he's something drug-users should steer clear of.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cheeky description: the fruit's juice interferes with how the body handles many prescription medicines.
explanation.definitionFit: Patients on statins and several other medicines are warned against this citrus fruit because its juice alters how the medication is metabolised.

clue.text: South American plant close to spectacular horse racing venue

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of spectacular
Aintree, near Liverpool, is the English racecourse that hosts the Grand National

explanation.surface: A tropical plant growing near a famous racecourse, as if spotted on a day at the races.
explanation.definitionFit: The rain tree is a large spreading tree of the pea family native to tropical South and Central America.

clue.text: Two irrational figures making food, in case

blocks.note: pi and e are the two most famous irrational numbers, written PI and E

explanation.surface: Two unreasonable people are somehow producing a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' sounds like a slur on the figures' character; in maths it means a number that cannot be written as a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie is a dish of filling baked inside a pastry shell, so it is literally edible matter enclosed in a crust.

clue.text: Parasite following follower of Mark

blocks.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
in the New Testament the Gospel of Luke comes right after the Gospel of Mark

explanation.surface: A parasitic creature trailing after a disciple of someone called Mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Flukes are flatworms that live as parasites inside host animals, the liver fluke being a well-known example.

clue.text: Less worried, taking year to probe American epic hero

indicators.note: something worried is agitated and tugged about, so its letters are mixed up
a probe goes inside something, so these letters are pushed into the next piece

blocks.note: US is the usual abbreviation for American
taken as written
Y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A calmer hero from an American epic, having taken a year off.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for less is shuffled together with the year letter, and that group then sits inside the abbreviation for American.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses is the Latin name of Odysseus, the wandering hero of Homer's epic poem the Odyssey.

clue.text: Conductor of musical work now popular after upturn

indicators.note: in a down clue an upturn turns the letters upside down, so they read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Tosca is Puccini's opera
in means fashionable, of the moment
in also means popular

explanation.surface: A musical work that has come back into fashion after a revival, with a conductor in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The two synonyms for fashionable come after the opera and are flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian orchestral and opera conductor, famously premiering several Puccini works.

clue.text: Able to steal a car

indicators.note: stealing means taking something in, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: fit means able or in a suitable state, as in fit to drive
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is quite capable of stealing a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiat is the Italian carmaker, and its name is used for the vehicles themselves.

clue.text: Is furious about grandma getting regularly barged around in horseplay

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fuming letters go round the rest
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the next word is kept
turned around means facing the other way, so the kept letters run backwards

blocks.note: someone who is furious fumes
nan is a familiar British word for a grandmother
the second, fourth and sixth letters of barged

explanation.surface: Someone is livid that granny has been shoved about during rough play.
explanation.walkthrough: The granny word is followed by the even letters of barged, turned back, and all of that sits inside the fuming verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Fun and games means playful, boisterous activity, exactly the rough-and-tumble larking about that horseplay describes.

clue.text: A flirt relaxed

blocks.note: taken as written
a tease is someone who flirts provocatively

explanation.surface: A flirtatious person in a laid-back mood.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a person free from tension or anxiety, and is also the military order to stand comfortably.

clue.text: Rescuer left one month before you returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so this word is read from right to left

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
I is the Roman numeral for one
FEB is the calendar abbreviation for February
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rescuer abandoned someone a month before the other person came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rescuer' looks like a person, but here it is a floating ring thrown to someone in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A buoyant ring thrown to a person in the water keeps them afloat and so saves them from drowning.

clue.text: Tennis star, one with vices

blocks.note: first meaning: Jannik ..., the Italian world number one tennis player
second meaning: a person who does wrong or transgresses

explanation.surface: A tennis star who turns out to have some bad habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Jannik Sinner is a leading Italian professional tennis player, and a sinner is generally someone who commits moral wrongs.

clue.text: Suppress outbursts about half-cut lech

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so the word is read backwards
cutting something in half removes part of it, so only the front half of the word stays

blocks.note: fits are sudden outbursts, as in fits of temper
taken as written

explanation.surface: Holding back angry outbursts about a tipsy lecher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it trims the lech in half.
explanation.definitionFit: To stifle is to hold back or smother something, such as a yawn or dissent, which is what suppressing means.

clue.text: Creepy sensation on skin in establishment infested with lice, essentially

indicators.note: something infested has creatures inside it, so the next letters are planted within
the essence of a word is its core, so only the middle letters are kept

blocks.note: a formation is the establishing or setting up of something
the middle two letters of lice

explanation.surface: A crawling feeling on the skin in a lice-ridden building.
explanation.walkthrough: The word comes from Latin formica, ant: the sensation is as if ants were crawling over the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term names a tactile hallucination of insects crawling on or under the skin.

clue.text: Mole caught: celebrity is aware

indicators.note: something caught by the ear has been heard, so the following words are taken by sound

blocks.note: a star is a celebrity
someone aware knows, which sounds like the facial feature

explanation.surface: A spy has been caught, and the famous person knows all about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' and 'caught' suggest a spy story, but the mole is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The star-nosed mole is a North American burrowing mammal with a ring of fleshy tentacles on its snout.

clue.text: New ginger nuts extremely brittle, with an indefinable quality

indicators.note: making something new means reshaping it, so the letters are rearranged
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its outer letters are kept

blocks.note: taken as written; gingernuts are hard British ginger biscuits
the first and last letters of brittle

explanation.surface: A fresh batch of ginger biscuits, very brittle, with some hard-to-pin-down quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' reads as describing the biscuits, but it is the signal to rearrange them.
explanation.definitionFit: Work that defies the conventions of any one category cannot be neatly classified, so its character resists definition.

clue.text: Claim mischievous child has marvellous revolutionary jargon

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so everything before this is read backwards

blocks.note: to bag is to claim, as in a British child shouting 'bags I'
an elf is a small mischievous creature, used of an impish child
fab is short for fabulous

explanation.surface: A cheeky kid says their fabulous revolutionary slogans are a claim to fame.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole charade of claim, child and marvellous is reversed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Bafflegab is North American slang for confusing, pompous official language designed to obscure meaning, a form of incomprehensible jargon.

clue.text: Local occasionally outbid me very quickly

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: a local is a British pub, and an inn is a pub
the first, third and fifth letters of outbid
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone at an auction keeps getting outbid by a person from the neighbourhood, all in a flash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like a neighbour; in Britain it is also the regular pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something happening almost instantly, taking practically no time at all, which is speedily.

clue.text: Mention fat in complex educational programme?

indicators.note: something complex is intricately tangled, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, twelve letters for rearranging

explanation.surface: A TV documentary that brings up dietary fat in a complicated way.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the definition is loose: such shows inform only in passing.
explanation.definitionFit: This genre of broadcasting blends factual information with entertainment, so it is a programme meant to teach while amusing.

clue.text: Restart argument, overcome by slight

indicators.note: something overcome is overwhelmed and engulfed, so it ends up inside the next word

blocks.note: slight means slim or thin
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A dispute over restarting something gets brushed aside by a minor snub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' reads as an insult, but it means slender.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, play resumes after the ball crosses the sideline by a player hurling it back onto the pitch.

clue.text: Unknown Scandinavian tackles international footballing legend

indicators.note: tackling means taking hold of, so the letters grip the next piece between them

blocks.note: Z is an algebraic unknown
a Dane is a Scandinavian from Denmark
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A mysterious Nordic player puts in a challenge on an international star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackles' fits the football surface, but it signals that one piece takes another inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinedine Zidane is a French former midfielder, a World Cup winner widely ranked among the greatest players ever.

clue.text: Detective Inspector Black beginning to restrain someone who stops things working

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is kept

blocks.note: DI is the abbreviation for Detective Inspector
sable is black in heraldry and poetry
the opening letter of restrain

explanation.surface: A police inspector named Black starts holding back a saboteur.
explanation.definitionFit: A disabler is an agent that renders something inoperative, such as a device that knocks out machinery.

clue.text: Panic, as hoodlum drinks resin

indicators.note: something drunk is held within, so the letters sit inside the surrounding words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A frightened thug is knocking back some resin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panic' looks like the definition; it is just part of the string the letters hide in.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashoo is a variant spelling of catechu, an astringent extract from acacia wood used in tanning and dyeing.

clue.text: Nothing stops search in ravine

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so this letter fills a space inside the next word

blocks.note: to comb is to search thoroughly
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing will halt the hunt down in the gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: A coomb, also spelt combe, is a short valley or hollow on a hillside, a narrow steep-sided cleft.

clue.text: Brave group of American lawyers?

blocks.note: a DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor
a ring is a group or gang

explanation.surface: Asking whether a gang of US lawyers counts as courageous.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the plural lawyers stands for a single abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the answer means bold and adventurous, willing to take risks, the same as courageous.

clue.text: Mystery wide brick?

blocks.note: W is the scoring abbreviation for a wide in cricket, a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach
a hod is the trough a builder carries bricks in, so a brick is jokingly one unit of a hod

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a wide brick.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whimsical idea of a brick as a single hod-load unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the informal name for a detective story built around discovering who committed the crime.

clue.text: They deliver emotional highs

blocks.note: first meaning: the American parcel delivery company United Parcel Service
second meaning: good times

explanation.surface: Something that brings people good moods.
explanation.definitionFit: The courier firm's initials name a parcel carrier, and in the plural phrase about life's fortunes they mean happy periods.

clue.text: Bird starts to tend eggs right now

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, so only those are kept from the following words

blocks.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A bird sets about incubating its eggs immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Terns are slender seabirds related to gulls, with forked tails and a habit of diving for fish.

clue.text: Almost crazy to describe boobs in salacious novel

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the next word is dropped
to describe can mean to draw a line around, so these letters enclose the next piece

blocks.note: bonkers is British slang for crazy
boobs are breasts, and a bust is a woman's chest

explanation.surface: It's almost mad how a racy book describes breasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boobs' could mean blunders, but here it is the bosom.
explanation.definitionFit: This British slang term names a popular blockbuster novel full of frequent explicit sex scenes, a racy page-turner.
